 JUDGMENT

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Sub Inspector of Srirampura police station against the accused No.1 and 2 C.C.32491/2018 for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 420, 511 r/w Sec.34 IPC and Secs. 3 and 7 of Essential Commodities Act 1955.

2. In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that on 24.03.2018 at about 9.00P.M, within the Parandama Hc-607 vs Suhas J on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85315921/
1 limits of Srirampura police station at Ramachandrapura 2nd main road where the accused No.1 and 2 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention were illegally transporting 52 bags of rice each weighing 50 kgs which supposed to be distributing to the BPL Card holders in their TATA ACE vehicle bearing KA-13-B-2320, by that time the C.W.1 received credible information about the said aspect and he has come to the said spot with the assistance of C.W.10, where verified and found that the accused No.1 and 2 transporting the said rice without any valid license and the accused with an intention to cheat the public and make unlawful gain transporting the same, therefore the C.W.1 has lodged the complaint against the accused No.1 and 2 before the Srirampura Police seeking necessary action against the accused in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.59/2018 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn, after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused No.1 and 2 , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, the accused No.1 and 2 were arrested and later C.C.32491/2018 enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused No.1 and 2, therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused No.1 and 2 in the language known to them, after understanding the same they denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial against the accused No.1 and 2.
5.

In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined 10 witnesses out of 12 charge sheeted witnesses, who are said to be complainant, mahazar witnesses, circumstantial witnesses as well as the investigating agency at P.W.1 to 10 and got marked eighteen documents at Ex.P-1 to P.18, during the period of prosecution evidence.

After completion of entire trial, this court has found that there were incriminating materials arising out against the accused No.1 and 2 , thereby statement of accused No.1 and 2 as required under Sec.313 of Cr.P.C., also recorded.

6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond obtained from the accused No.1 and 2.
7.

During the course of arguments, the following citations relied by the counsel for accused:
1. 2013(1) KCCR 398,
2. 2015(2) KCCR 1345,
Parandama Hc-607 vs Suhas J on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85315921/
2 3.
Crl.Petition No.9842/2016 8.

In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 24.03.2018 at about 9.00P.M, within the limits of Srirampura police station at C.C.32491/2018 Ramachandrapura 2nd main road where the accused No.1 and 2 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention were illegally transporting 52 bags of rice each weighing 50 kgs which supposed to be distributing to the BPL Card holders in their TATA ACE vehicle bearing KA-13-B-2320, by that time the C.W.1 received credible information about the said aspect and he has come to the said spot with the assistance of C.W.10, where verified and found that the accused No.1 and 2 transporting the said rice without any valid license and thereby the accused No.1 and 2 has committed the offences punishable U/Sec.3 and 7 of Essential commodities Act?
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above mentioned date, place and time the accused No.1 and 2 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention in order to cheat the public and gain profit by selling the rice to the public , which was given to the BPL Card holders by the Government and thereby the accused persons have committed an offence of "cheating" punishable U/s 420 r/w Sec.34 of IPC?"
3.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above mentioned date, place and time the accused No.1 and 2 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention, did not comply the directions of the Government to distribte the rice to BPL Card holders and were attempting to transport the said rice for selling it to the public and thereby the accused persons have committed an offence punishable U/s 511 r/w Sec.34 of IPC?"
4. What Order?
9. My answer to the above points are as under:
Point No.1 to 3 : In the 'Negative' C.C.32491/2018 Point No.4: As per the final order,
for the following:-
REASONS 10. Point Nos.1 to 3: These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.
Parandama Hc-607 vs Suhas J on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85315921/
3 11. In order to prove its case the prosecution has examined in total 10 witnesses out of the 12 charge sheeted witnesses along with Ex.P.1 to 18, among them two witnesses ie C.W.4 and 5 were ordered to be dropped.

As far as documentary testimonials are concerned Ex.P.1 is the requisition/
complaint which has been lodged on 24.03.2018, same has been registered under Cr.No.59/2018 for the alleged offences punishable U/Sec. 3 and 7 of Essential Commodities Act in which it is mentioned that on 24.03.2018 when they were discharging their duty at 2nd main road,
Ramachandrapura, by that time the accused were apprehended along with material objects,
subsequently registered the case.
Ex.P.2 to 5 are photos of the alleged vehicle.
Ex.P.6 is the seizure mahazar which drawn on 25.03.2018 at about 9.00 A.M to 10.00A.M at Srirampura PS, rest of the documents is concerned Ex
. P.7 -statement of witness by name Vasudevan S/o.Late.Muniswamy,
Ex.P.8 is the request letter dated 16.04.2018 which placed before RTO seeking information about the alleged vehicle, Ex.P9 is the B extract concerned to the said vehicle.
Ex.P.10 is the FIR, Ex.P.11 and 12 are the permission letters which placed before D.C and court,

Ex.P.13 is the order dated 10.04.2018, Ex.P.14- letter dated 13.04.2018, Ex.P.15 is the letter dated 07.05.2018 which placed before Food Inspector, Ex.P.16 is the letter dated 27.04.2018, Ex.P.17 -Notification dated15.05.2018,
Ex.P.18 is the acknowledgement dated 17.05.2018.
All these documents which clearly establishes that undoubtedly 52 rice bags weighing 50 kgs each have been seized as per Ex.P.6 on 25.03.2018.

Later on they have been handed over the same to the concerned authority in accordance with law,
but herein the question that would arise before this court is C.C.32491/2018 that whether the accused persons have been committed these alleged offences as alleged in the charge sheet.
12.

In this regard on going through the oral evidence of prosecution witnesses in which it is clearly shows that as per say of P.W.1 the accused persons along with the rice bags have been seized from the custody of accused persons, in other words it had been said that due to suspect of these accused persons they have been brought the accused to the police station at about 9.30 P.M, in fact they did not verify how many bags were in the said vehicle.

On this point itself the accused counsel rendered arguments that as on the date of alleged incident simply the accused persons have been brought to the police station due to the reason behind is that they have not given mamuli amount.
Moreover these accused persons are just running the vehicle on the basis of hire for their livelihood and there is no connection between the accused as well as the rice bags.
In fact at the moment of apprehension, admittedly the P.W.1 also has not seen any rice bags in the said vehicle.
If so he would certainly looked into the said vehicle.

Not only the above said reason, the complainant police have brought the said vehicle to the police station around 9.30P.M, by that time neither the concerned police nor their higher authority did not taken any action against the vehicle as well as the accused persons that itself leads to show that some unknown hands have played fraud in the night hours without the knowledge of accused persons, therefore the concerned police have made deliberate mistake for the reasons best known to them.

Per contra P.W.2, 3 and 5 who said to be seizure and spot mahazar witnesses did not support to the case of prosecution and hence here suspicion that would commonly arisen upon the said seizure of 52 rice bags, in support of which the P.W.5 who has deposed in his evidence is as below :

4

13.

By virtue of these admissions itself, here there is no doubt as per say of P.W8 and P.W.10, those alleged rice bags belongs to the Government, but it is relevant to mention here that from whom those rice bags have been brought, that thing has not been proven by the prosecution, in addition to that C.W.4 and 5 who are owners of the Ramachandra Sahakara Sangha Society not been secured before the court even though they are very much available in the said locality, these aspects are showing that the prosecution has failed to fulfill those ommissions.

Now coming to the vehicle,
here also there is no dispute, as per Ex.P.9 it belongs to one Allabhakash S/o.
Hussain khan, who is none other than accused No.2 and there is a doubt that the prosecution has not been proven that as on the date of alleged commission of offence,
in this vehicle those rice bags have been transporting or not because the IO as well as the P.W.5 saying that he did not investigated that those rice bags have been transporting or not?

That point itself going to show that even the P.W.5 does not know how many rice bags were allegedly transporting in the said vehicle and where those rice bags were brought so as to know that whether these exclusively belongs to the Government, supposed to be distributed to the BPL card holders.

Merely on the oral statement of these witnesses it cannot be believed C.C.32491/2018 that these rice bags are belongs to the Government, this extent of doubt also not been clearly proven, in addition to that no such documents are available in the case file that from whom and where they may going to sell the rice for higher price, however this court feels that these are only assumptive and fictionate reasons that these rice bags are belongs to Government.

Therefore this court is of the considered opinion that on considering the law laid down in the foregoing decisions and even after providing sufficient time so as to prove its case the prosecution has failed to do so as to how the accused tried to cheat the Government.
Based on these reasons no such incriminating materials are forthcoming against the accused persons for which accused cannot be convicted for the foregoing reasons.
Hence obviously benefit of doubt goes to the accused persons.
Hence I answer point no.1 to 3 in the Negative.
14. Point No.4;

In view of my findings on point No.1 to 3 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused No.1 and 2 are not found guilty and they are hereby acquitted of the offences puishable under Sec.420, 511 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 7 of Essential Commodities Act.
Parandama Hc-607 vs Suhas J on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85315921/
5 The bail bond executed by the accused No.1 and 2 stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused No.1 and 2 is ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
The property seized as per P.F.No.28/2018 item No.2 is already disposed off, same is made absolute.
